column1: I idolize a particular hero of my faith, and constantly refer to that person’s deeds and example.
I can find common ground between the fiercest enemies, empathizing with them and always working toward peace.
I see omens in every event and action. The gods try to speak to us, we just need to listen.
Nothing can shake my optimistic attitude.
I quote (or misquote) sacred texts and proverbs in almost every situation.
I am tolerant (or intolerant) of other faiths and respect (or condemn) the worship of other gods.
I’ve enjoyed fine food, drink, and high society among my temple’s elite. Rough living grates on me.
I’ve spent so long in the temple that I have little practical experience dealing with people in the outside world.
I know and can reproduce every type of birdsong in the forest.
I’m more sympathetic to the plight of an animal than to a person’s.
I grin from ear to ear whenever I see baby animals, especially kittens.
When I kill an animal, I use every last bit of it, leaving nothing to waste.
I always tend to my mount’s needs at the end of a long trip before my own.
I prefer the company of animals over people and respond to attempts at chit chat with grunts rather than words.
I know that I studied at the world’s greatest academies and think little of those who learned elsewhere.
I am eager to spread my knowledge and will happily share with those who wish to learn.
I am a curmudgeon and lash out at those who irritate me.
I don’t actually care for antiques, but it’s a great way to make money.
I am quite stingy with my knowledge and share it only with those I deem worthy.
I prefer the company of my antiques to that of people.
I’ll do whatever it takes to win, even cheat, because winning means survival.
I don’t back down from a fight—that’s a sign of weakness.
Everybody meets their match sooner or later.
I can always find work, whether I need to move bricks or defend a farmstead.
I regret every person I was forced to kill in the arena and will take revenge against those responsible eventually.
I’m tight with my money because I know the real price of it.
I’m pleasant enough, at least until you try pushing me around and taking advantage of me.
Live free, because you never know if tomorrow will be the day they cut you down.
I am haunted by the horrors of war.
I am loud and boisterous.
I feel bitter resentment towards the Empire for conquering my people.
I always follow the rules, even against my interests.
I take great pride in my physical prowess.
I look for insult where none was given.
I believe in the philosophy “live and let live”.
I prefer to stay busy. Downtime makes me restless.
I have a sweet tooth. You can bribe me with sweets any day.
I face my fears head on- the threat of a little pain doesn’t stop me!
I love nature…it really does provide everything we need to survive.
I believe a little bit of preparation can avoid a lot of unpleasantness later on.
I am fanatically loyal to my cult.
I wish to spread the word of Chaos to the masses.
I hate humanity and wish to see it punished.
The gods are false; in Chaos I know we will all be equal.
I seek to harness Chaos for my own power.
I have second thoughts about what I am doing.
I am the best there is and I will prove it.
I enjoy training new athletes looking to compete.
I always ask those who best me for advice on how to improve.
I am spiteful towards any who beat me in competition.
I am very jovial and enjoy celebrating with my fellows.
I spend all my free time training.
I’m very shy.
I am incredibly outgoing in my personal and professional lives.
I want for a life of comfort and plenty.
I know I’m beautiful and will use it to get what I want.
I am embarrassed to tell others of my past.
I am proud of my profession, no matter how others see me.
Unless I must speak, I hold my breath while serving others.
It takes all my effort not to show the effusive emotions I feel when I help others. Best to quietly serve.
It’s getting harder to tolerate the prejudices of those I serve daily.
Though the old ways are hard to give up, I want to be my own boss. I’ll decide my path.
Serving my family and friends is the only thing I truly care about.
City life is killing my soul. I long for the old courtly ways.
It’s time for my fellows to wake up and be taken advantage of no longer.

It’s the small things that make it all worthwhile.
I try to be present in every moment.
I don’t shy away from battle, even when I think I might be somewhat overmatched.
I constantly keep an eye on my valuables. I don’t trust even my closest friends
Why would I worry about the future when I have to survive today?
I’ve seen things out here that just shouldn’t exist… not in this realm, or any other.
You can’t survive the desert unless you know its inhabitants, and how to survive them.
I like to help people who seem lost or helpless.
The one thing that keeps me going is my faith in my god or pantheon.
Sometimes the best way to resolve differences with a stranger is to insult them well.
I’m much happier sleeping under the stars than in a bed in a stuffy caravanserai.
It’s always best to help a traveler in need; one day it might be you.
I am slow to trust strangers, but I’m extremely loyal to my friends.
If there’s a camel race, I’m the first to saddle up!
I always have a tale or poem to share at the campfire.
I don’t like sleeping in the same place more than two nights in a row.
I’ve been troubled by dreams for the last month. I am determined to uncover their meaning.
I feel lonelier in a crowded city than I do out on the empty desert sands.
I’m eager to find this destiny and move on with the next stage in my life.
I keep the fire of my hope burning bright. I’m sure this will work out for the best.
Fate has a way of finding you no matter what you do. I’m resigned to whatever they have planned for me, but I’ll enjoy my time on the way.
I owe it to myself or to those who helped establish this destiny. I’m determined to follow this through to the end.
I don’t know what this path means for me or my future. I’m more afraid of going back to that destiny than of seeing what’s out in the world.
I didn’t ask for this, and I don’t want it. I’m bitter that I must change my life for it.
Few have been chosen to complete this lifepath, and I’m proud to be one of them.
Who can say how this will work out? The world is an uncertain place, and I’ll find my destiny when it finds me.
I like to travel, meet new people, and learn about different customs.
I intercede in minor squabbles to find common ground on all sides.
I never disparage others, even when they might deserve such treatment.
I always try to make a new friend wherever I travel, and when I return to those areas, I seek out my friends.
I have learned how to damn with faint praise, but I only use it when someone has irked me.
I am not opposed to throwing a bit of coin around to ensure a good first impression.
Even when words fail at the outset, I still try to calm tempers.
I treat everyone as an equal, and I encourage others to do likewise.
I eat my nails when I am nervous.
My answers are always in the form of a question.
I always keep an eye on the way out.
I am curious and attracted to macabre things.
When I stare into someone’s eyes, I never look away, and I never blink.
The suffering of others leaves me seemingly indifferent.
I tend to dress in black only.
During idle moments I tend to fiddle with knives and other blades.
I like to slip into cramped spaces where no one can reach me.
I like to caress the ground or rock walls.
I never face problems directly, I always look for a winding path and yet safer, in my opinion.
I think anyone who is nice to me has a second purpose.
I have lost a lot of friends; I do not want to lose any more.
Teamwork is the best way to achieve a goal.
I’m always ecstatic at the sight of the moon.
Bright lights bother my eyes.
I am loud and jovial to the point of annoyance.
I am happy to escort those who would otherwise never survive the desert.
I am a social person and don’t like traveling the desert alone.
I am a loner and prefer my own company.
I actually hate the sand!
I want to see every desert in the world.
I take pride in my knowledge of the healing arts.
I meditate to balance my own energies at least once a day.
I believe what we put into our bodies and absorb with our minds affects our overall well-being, so I extol the benefits of healthy eating, exercise, and meditation every chance I get.
I am an excellent listener and information gatherer- skills I’ve developed to determine the root of a patient’s health challenge.
I’m a touchy-feely person, always trying to sense the elemental energies flowing through a person’s body.
I prefer living as close to nature as possible so my elemental energies are less likely to be sullied by impurities.
I always note potential escape routes in any situation.
I prefer to listen and observe – its’ remarkable what you can learn that way.
I love to learn new facts and experience new things.
I always eat as much as I can when I get the chance.
I refuse to work for free.
I wear the scars of my forced servitude openly. I am not ashamed of my past.
Those who earn my trust can count on me, no matter what.
People underestimate me, but that just gives me an advantage over them.
I will never forget what life was like before exile. I frequently reminisce and maintain traditions.
I still worry about my family and friends back home.
Despite my exile, I am still fiercely loyal to my community.
I have learned a great deal from my time in the wilderness.
My hard life in exile has left me with no desire for material possessions.
With nothing left to lose, I can take every risk.
I never liked those people anyway.
If I can handle exile, I can handle anything.
I know the lore of the farm/herd; let me tell you about it.
Whenever I visit a new place, I always notice the crops, animals, and soil.
My farm is a business and I’m trying to expand.
Early to bed, early to rise; I get more done before 6 AM than the army.
I prefer stability, consistency, and predictability, like the seasons.
I am competitive with other farmers and always try to have the biggest and best produce at harvest time.
I am more comfortable around plants and animals than people.
I see omens in weather patterns and animal behaviors.
I will never forget being hungry in the winter. I field dress beasts that fall to blade or arrow so that I am never hungry again.
I may be alone in the forest, but I am only ever lonely in cities.
Walking barefoot allows me to interact more intuitively with the natural world.
The road is just another kind of wall. I make my own paths and go where I will.
Others seek the gods in temples and shrines, but I know their will is only revealed in the natural world, not an edifice constructed by socalled worshippers. I pray in the woods, never indoors.
What you call personal hygiene, I call an artificially imposed distraction from natural living.
No forged weapon can replace the sheer joy of a kill accomplished only with hands and teeth.
Time lived alone has made me accustomed to talking loudly to myself, something I still do even when others are present.
I have a thousand stories about every aspect of the adventuring life.
My past is my own, and to the pit with anyone who pushes me about it.
I can endure any hardship without complaint.
I have a list of rules for surviving adventures, and I refer to them often.
It’s a dangerous job, and I take my pleasures when I can.
I can’t help mentioning all the famous friends I’ve met before.
Anyone who doesn’t recognize me is clearly not someone worth knowing.
I’ve seen it all. If you don’t listen to me, you’re going to get us all killed.
I’m happiest when I’m on a gently rocking vessel, staring at the distant horizon.
Every time we hoisted the mainsail and raised the pirate flag, I felt butterflies in my stomach.
I have lovers in a dozen different ports. Most of them don’t know about the others.
Being a pirate has taught me more swear words and bawdy jokes than I ever knew existed. I like to try them out when I meet new people.
One day I hope to have enough gold to fill a tub so I can bathe in it.
There’s nothing I enjoy more than a good scrap—the bloodier, the better.
When a storm is blowing and the rain is lashing the deck, I’ll be out there getting drenched. It makes me feel so alive!
Nothing makes me more annoyed than a badly tied knot.
Nature has lessons to teach us all, and I’m always happy to share them.
Once while out on a hunt, something happened which was very relatable to our current situation. Let me tell you about it.
My friends are my new charges, and I’ll make sure they thrive.
Preparation and knowledge are the key to any success.
I’ve dealt with all sorts of wealthy and noble folk, and I’ve seen just how spoiled they can be.
I feel like my animals are the only ones who really understand me.
You can train yourself to accomplish anything you put your mind to accomplishing.
The world shows you everything you need to know to understand a situation. You just have to be paying attention to the details.
I never raise my voice, always speaking calmly, seemingly devoid of any emotion.
I have the utmost respect and veneration for the legacies of those who have passed before us.
The dead are dead; they don’t need their stuff. I need their stuff.
I always carry multiple wards, charms, and holy symbols with me, for the undead are everywhere.
I am secretive about myself and my past, and I make friends slowly, if at all.
I am bright and optimistic, and I revel in the joy and vigor of life in spite of (or because of) my somewhat morbid past.
I am constantly commenting, scrutinizing, and jotting down notes on anything regarding tombs, burial rites, and histories of the dead.
I am used to being the smartest (only) person in the room; I therefore take great pains to explain the obvious to the obviously uninformed.
My breath smells like mint leaves.
I can name every plant in the forest.
I’m always gnawing on a blade of grass.
No one can whip up a tastier salad than I can.
I enjoy nothing more than rich soil and growing my own food.
I’m a strict vegetarian. I don’t understand why anyone would choose to eat dead animal flesh when there’s so much variety to choose from in the plant kingdom.
I seek the company of like-minded folk.
I am eager to spread my knowledge and will happily share with those who wish to learn.
I get nervous when I am not in the safety of the forest.
I am dour and mournful.
I am quite stingy with my knowledge and share it only with those I deem worthy.
I prefer the company of trees to people.
We should probably hear out our enemies, who knows what they’re going through.
I’m confused about my place in the world and am looking for guidance.
I apologize to everyone I meet, even those who have no idea of my shady past.
I am extremely literal and have trouble understanding anything beyond cold logic.
A little light thievery never hurt anybody.
After being an evil henchman for so long, I’m not certain how to make decisions for myself.
I am constantly looking over my shoulder for enemies from my past.
I need someone to acknowledge all these good deeds I keep doing, otherwise I might stop.
I can tell if you are virtuous or not based on how my horse reacts to you.
There are no riches greater than a healthy horse and the wide-open plains.
Making war is one of the main reasons we live. I ride into battle without fear.
I don’t trust folk from the city. I tolerate them because I must.
I have never smelled anything so foul as when I visited my first city.
I will not steal from you, but if you have something I need, I will battle you for it.
I never delighted in anything so much as when I came upon the cities.
I do not grow loud or angry when you cross me. I simply ride you down and kill you.
City dwellers think I’m simple. Their mistake. But I know I can’t trust them.
It’s not the number of foes who stand against me, but the number of bodies I’ll leave dead on the field.
Drink deep from the cup of life, for we only live once and we’ll never be back this way again.
Challenge me and it will be the last mistake you make.
Cities are filled with false magnificence, for the towers, halls, and buildings cannot compare to the majesty of the mountains, trees, and rivers.
I fear no man, nor beast, nor monster, for the worst they can do is kill me, and death is not a thing to be feared.
Gods are powerful, but they care not for the concerns of men.
Nothing is better than seeing your enemies slain on the field of battle.
I love being in the wilderness, stalking prey in the early dawn.
I have the worst luck of any hunter I know.
I love tales of hunting and wilderness adventure, let me tell you one.
I am always evaluating other people’s hunting skills and comparing them to my own.
In every aspect of my life I am a consummate stalker, patient and deadly.
I feel a little sad for people who rely on the butcher for their meat.
I am an expert on the tools of my trade and love to share my knowledge.
I obsess about preparedness and constantly check my equipment.
I am haunted by the failures of the past.
I boast about my great military feats and sometimes other people’s.
I feel bitter resentment towards the symbols of the old Empire.
I protect the weak, no matter the cost.
I’ll fight any battle anywhere for the right coin.
I’ll never draw my blade first and only do so in defense.
I am quick to anger and quicker to draw blades.
I am filled with hatred for those who broke the Empire.
I insist on doing all the cooking, and I plan strategies like I cook—with proper measurements and all the right ingredients.
Lending a sympathetic ear or a shoulder to cry on often yields unexpected benefits.
I always have a story or tale to relate to any situation.
There is a world of tastes and flavors to explore.
Few problems can’t be solved with judicious application of a stout cudgel.
I never pass up the chance to bargain. Never.
I demand the finest accommodations; I know what they’re worth.
I can defuse a situation with a joke, cutting remark, or arched eyebrow.
I was tricked into servitude in my younger years. Now, I bow to no master, not even the laws of reality.
I have seen the cracks in what we perceive as truth. I want to expand those cracks by any means.
I love the rush I get from discovering something new. It’s an addiction.
I am tired of being caught in the tangle of other’s lives. I want to break free of their mental weakness.
In the grand scheme of things, nothing we do matters. Let’s make our own meanings.
I crave power above all else and I will take my research to terrible lengths to get it.
If we don’t teach the future generation everything we know; they will suffer the same as we do.
Magic is silly and fake; I can prove it too.
I am loud, crass, and mean, and that’s just the way I like it.
A sharp mind and a fast tongue is the best way to stay out of danger.
I love the thrill of combat and don’t think I could live without it.
If I have gold in my pouch and a lover (or two) at my side then I am happy.
I am deeply political and sometimes object to the jobs I must do.
This is a fun gig, but what I’d really like to do is have a farm.
I will give all to those around me suffering, even if I caused the suffering.
I won’t take a job without knowing every detail.
I am ashamed of my family’s reputation and seek to distance myself from their deeds.
I have seen the world and know people everywhere.
I expect the best life has to offer and won’t settle for less.
I know stories from a thousand campaigns and can apply them to any situation.
After too many betrayals, I don’t trust anyone.
My parents were heroes, and I try to live up to their example.
I have seen the horrors of war; nothing disturbs me anymore.
I truly believe I have a destiny of glory and fame awaiting me.
I am thrilled by the thought of an upcoming fight.
Why wait until I’m famous to have songs written about me? I can write my own right now!
I know many stories and legends of famous adventurers and compare everything to these tales.
Humor is how I deal with fear.
I always seek to learn new ways to use my weapons and love sharing my knowledge.
The only way I can prove myself is to work hard and take risks.
When you stop training, you sign your own death notice.
I try to act braver than I actually am.
I’m a pacifist at heart and hate any sort of confrontation.
The best information can’t be bought. It must be found by exploring.
I am obsessed with a specific type of monster and will risk everything to just get close to them.
My prestigious upbringing makes me loathe getting myself dirty and I’ll complain about it profusely.
I have no pity for the animals I study. They are dangerous creatures and if some must die to understand them, so be it.
I tend to want to revisit my favorite monster dens over and over, even if the monsters have long since left or died.
The monsters may have it right. I am constantly comparing civilized life to that of the monsters.
I’m really just using this as an excuse to hunt down the most exotic monsters for sport.
I don’t eat my friends (at least not while they are alive). My foes, on the other hand…
Meeting another’s gaze is a challenge for dominance that I never fail to answer.
Monsters I understand; people are confusing.
There are two types of creatures in life: prey or not-prey.
I often use the growls, sounds, or calls of my adopted parents instead of words.
Inconsequential items fascinate me.
It's not my fault, I was raised by ['wolves'|'fairies'|'werewolves'|'orcs'|'the lizardfolk'|'troglodytes'|'merfolk'].
I may look fine, but I behave like a monster.
I’m always humming a song, but I can’t remember the words.
I love learning new things and meeting new people.
I want to prove my worth and have people know my name.
I don’t like places that are crowded or noisy.
I’m mistrustful of mages and magic in general.
I like to keep everything tidy and organized so that I can find things easily.
Every night I record my day in a detailed journal.
I live in the present. The future will come as it may.
I had to organize other survivors or die. I seize the initiative whenever my group’s direction is in doubt.
I would have been lost forever without an elder survivor. I constantly mimic or refer to that person’s example.
I had to move quickly to make it this far. I keep interactions short and businesslike.
Giving up spells doom in my experience. I avoid dwelling on bad possibilities.
I came up with handy rhymes, mottoes, or rules to keep my head on straight. I quote them at any opportunity.
I know better than to trust what my eyes see. I always verify.
I can't trust any benevolent power after what I experienced.

There are things I regret learning, so I take extra care to ensure others need to know before telling them potentially unsettling things. I use euphemisms or vague summaries rather than getting into details.
I will accept any dare and expect accolades when I complete it.
Revelry and boisterousness are for foolish children. I prefer to quietly wait and watch.
I am more than a match for any northern reaver. If they believe that is not so, let them show me what stuff they are made of.
I yearn for the raiding season and the tales of blood and butchery I can use to draw the crowds.
Ragnarok is nigh. I will bear witness to the end of all things and leave a record should there be any who survive it.
There is nothing better than mutton, honeyed mead, and a crowd in thrall to my words.
The gods weave our fates. There is nothing to do but accept this and live as we will.
All life is artifice. I lie better than most and I am not ashamed to reap the rewards.
I always ask questions, especially if I think I can learn something new.
I believe every superstition I hear and follow their rules fanatically.
The things I know give me nightmares, and not only when I sleep.
Nothing makes me happier than explaining some obscure lore to my friends.
I startle easily.
I perform a host of rituals throughout the day that I believe protect me from occult threats.
I never know when to give up.
The more someone refuses to believe me, the more I am determined to convince them.
When not in battle, I’m even tempered, and I have no problem sitting in the saddle for days at a time.
I refuse to regret the things I’ve done in the past, for I cannot change them.
Insult me again and you’ll be wearing your sword through your guts.
I keep to myself unless I have a reason to speak to people, 5 If I make you a promise, I will deliver, or I’ll die trying.
I’m always loud, and I I see no reason to hold back with my thoughts.
Drink with me tonight, for tomorrow we may die!
Watch how you talk to my mount. I’ll become angry as though it were me you’re talking to.
I am forlorn and my music carries a haunting melody.
I never hold my tongue when it comes to bragging about my own exploits.
I hold great resentment for those whom I perform for, wishing I was one of them.
I cannot stand being second best and will do whatever I can to stay on top.
I’ll perform any ballad anywhere for the right coin.
I love to share my arts, even with those too illoff to afford me.
I am adept at defusing situations before they turn violent.
My temper can flare, especially when my work is insulted.
I do not deal in absolutes. There is a solution to every problem, an answer for every riddle.
I am used to associating with educated and “elevated” society. I find rough living and rough manners unpalatable.
Years spent witnessing the dealings, intrigues, and industrial espionage of the Bouquet Districts’ mercantile-elite have left me secretive and guarded.
I have a strong interest and sense for fashion and current trends.
I eagerly discuss the minutiae, subtleties, and nuances of my profession to any who will listen.
I am easily distracted by unusual or exceptional botanical specimens.
I can seem distant and introverted. I listen more than I speak.
I always strive to make allies, not enemies.
I know I am above those of lesser birth and will flaunt it openly.
I fear losing my position in this world.
I rarely travel, anything important can come to me.
I seek to help those less fortunate than myself.
I am very generous with my coin.
I am incredibly stingy.
I am consumed with a desire to see and experience new things.
I bond quickly to new friends and lose those bonds just as quickly should we be separated.
I constantly compare what I am seeing to what I have seen or experienced before.
I have heard a story about everything and will tell you if you do not stop me.
I feel uncomfortable staying in one place for too long.
I always travel light—anything I cannot carry is something I do not need.
I am always looking around as if everything is new and I trust none of it.
I know that anything is possible, so I am quick to believe almost anything.
I am constantly rushing through conversations, trying to pull all the important details so I can keep questing.
I rush in, no matter the situation, context, or consequences.
This is not the body I remember, and it presents some interesting new challenges for me.
My lust for loot is insatiable. I’m worse than most dragons.
I am careless with my equipment, using potions flippantly and mistreating magical artifacts.
I am hyper competitive, pushing myself to terrible limits to come out on top.
I make sound effects for my movements and label my attacks with cool sounding names.
I can’t help but poke my nose where it doesn’t belong.
I know that I trained at the world’s greatest theatres and think little of those who learned elsewhere.
I have lost myself in my work and often have difficulty separating reality from the stage.
I dote on my actors like an overbearing father.
I have played so many characters that I sometimes lose track of who I am.
I have great resentment for playwrights who garner more success than I do.
I greatly prefer writing plays to acting in them.
I enjoy running.
I can walk for hours without tiring.
I love challenging people to arm wrestling competitions.
I have something for every possible need in my backpack.
I like the challenge of finding ways around difficult terrain.
I lift a series of heavy objects every morning to stay conditioned.
I am the best around. No one will ever keep me down.
I am constantly amazed that people enjoy what I do and personally thank everyone for supporting me.
I love teaching those around me whatever I know but I’m not always good at it.
People are strange. I don’t know what they want from me. Best just to work.
I pour so much into my work that sometimes I forget to sleep or eat.
My mind is constantly wandering, making concentrating on anything difficult.
I have a tendency to ramble on about the things that interest me, even if nobody is there to ramble to.
I would rather do anything else than what people know me for, but I am no good at anything else.
I believe in providing the best possible service to my clients.
I have an inquisitive mind and love facts and details.
I’m arrogant about my job and the status it provides.
I can quote all the famous philosophers and quite a few infamous ones as well.
I’m contemptuous of people who can’t keep up with my intellectual conversation.
I can talk for hours about my profession.
I sometimes donate my service to worthy clients.
I expect my professional reputation precedes me by now, and I am surprised when I meet people who don’t know of my achievements.
I don’t put up with people’s disrespect. I’ll beat them bloody!
It will be a long time before I can deal with my past.
I don’t need to atone. I was just trying to survive, like anyone else.
Fear of being discovered guides so many of my actions.
Say what you want of my past, I know how to fight, and I can use that.
I’ll take whatever job you have for me, no questions asked. Just do the same for me.
I may not prey on travelers anymore, but if I see something of yours that I want, I’m going to get it.
If I go far enough away, I can outrun my past.
I drop mentions of my past-life recollections into casual conversation.
I’m rightly considered an “old soul” by many.
I have the kind of zest for life and all that it has to offer of someone who understands how brief it all is.
I only reveal that I am reawakened to people I know I can trust, especially if I feel a past-life connection.
I often become lost in reveries of my old memories, seeming distant and distracted.
Although I do not seek it, I do not fear death, but I consider the undead terrible abominations.
I have a measure of calm and serenity far greater than my years.
My experience has made me a bit world-weary and sarcastic.
I am not accountable for my behavior; society has created me.
If everyone saw the world the way I see it, then it would be a much better place.
I spit in the face of any noble I encounter, regardless of the consequences.
I am a natural born leader and often command small groups of people like myself.
I love tagging anything I can with my art or symbol.
My words never seem to come out right and it often gets me into trouble.
I think I could be someone great, but I am unwilling to put in the effort required.
I don’t understand subtlety, nuance, or tact. Say what you mean or don’t bother saying it at all.
I am always prepared for the worst because I know what it can be like.
I am exceptionally proud of my homeland and heritage and carry them with me always.
Having suffered and lost, I am always kind to others in similar straits.
